Repo: /opt/nxeon-v2, branch design/v2 — a from-scratch visual redesign ("Nexion") of the real Nxeon hosting platform, running sandboxed (NXEON_SANDBOX=1: real DB and code paths, no VM ever provisions, no card ever charges). Read /opt/nxeon-v2/CLAUDE.md FIRST for the operating rules (never build in /opt/nxeon, never pkill -f by pattern, verification-by-screenshot discipline, etc). Login: customer@nxeon.local / wGPZqhCbsLdz (see /root/nxeon-v2-credentials.txt), base URL https://v2.q4w8zt3ky6vn2sm.nxeon.cloud.

NOTE: a previous attempt at this exact task stalled out and made zero edits — it seems to have gotten confused waiting on some kind of "rebuild lock" from a sibling process and gave up instead of just proceeding. There is no such lock you need to wait on. Just do the work directly: edit, typecheck, rebuild when you want to verify, screenshot, move on. Don't wait for anything external to signal you.

CONTEXT — a long session just finished building a light theme for this whole dashboard (dark was the only mode before; light is new, toggled via `data-theme="light"` on `<html>`, tokens as `--color-*` CSS custom properties in app/globals.css) and found/fixed a long tail of bugs across most pages. Three OTHER parallel agents are simultaneously auditing different pages elsewhere in this same tree right now. COORDINATION: you may rebuild (./rebuild.sh) and restart the nxeon-v2-web service as needed for your own verification — just don't leave it down when you finish, and do NOT create git commits (the orchestrating session commits everyone's work together). Stay within your assigned pages/files (listed below) so you don't collide with the other agents.

YOUR PAGES: /dashboard/ssl, /dashboard/volumes, /dashboard/sites, /dashboard/nxcloud, /dashboard/tools, /dashboard/migrate, /dashboard/projects. Find each one's page component (app/dashboard/<name>/page.tsx, which will import a components/nx/<Name>View.tsx or components/customer/<name>/* — grep to find it) and any sub-tabs/modals it opens.

THE BUG TAXONOMY TO CHECK FOR ON EVERY PAGE (all of these have been found and fixed repeatedly elsewhere this session — you're checking whether the same mistakes exist on your assigned pages):
1. A literal hardcoded color (hex or rgba, e.g. `bg-[rgba(10,22,48,.5)]`, `text-[#7f9ad0]`) used for something that should adapt between themes, instead of the theme's own `--color-*` tokens / `text-tx`, `text-tx-dim`, `text-tx-faint`, `border-rim-hi`, `bg-well`, `bg-surface`, `.card`/`.card-glass`, etc. (grep app/globals.css for the full token list). On the light page these often render as either invisible-on-invisible or a jarring leftover dark box.
2. A hero/banner section with its own fixed dark background + `text-white` heading — if it's not wrapped in the `.nx-dark-island` CSS class (also in app/globals.css), light mode's generic fix flips `text-white` to dark ink, making it invisible against a scrim that stayed dark on purpose. Look for `<header>` or hero `<div>`s with a literal dark gradient background.
3. `bg-white` (bare, not `bg-white/NN`) used to mean "always paint this literally white" (e.g. a toggle switch knob, an active-segment pill) — this breaks because `--color-white` now means "ink" in light mode. Fix: literal `bg-[#fff]` if it must always be bright regardless of theme, or a proper light-mode-aware treatment otherwise.
4. An `Icon` component (components/nx/Icon.tsx) rendered with no `tone` prop inside a colored/gradient badge that has an intended contrasting text color set on the wrapper — the icon overrides that intended color with its own default tone class instead of inheriting it. Fix: pass `tone="inherit"`.
5. `text-white/NN` (opacity-modified) sitting on something that is NOT actually a light-mode-adapted surface (e.g. its own literal-color decorative card) — gets wrongly retargeted by the global opacity-decoupling rule meant for text sitting on the actual page background.
6. Any canvas/backdrop using `globalCompositeOperation = "lighter"` or CSS `mix-blend-screen`/`mix-blend-lighten` — these only ever add light and wash to grey on a light page. If you find one NOT already using components/nx/auroraTheme.ts's `isLightTheme()`/`auroraComposite()`/`auroraStrandGradient()` helpers, wire it in (read components/nx/DomainsAurora.tsx as a working example of the pattern) rather than reinventing the fix.
7. A `.card-on`-style "selected" state, or any custom selected/active-state styling, that renders as a solid dark block regardless of theme — should look intentional (accent border/glow) rather than like a hole punched in an otherwise light page.
8. Genuine FUNCTIONAL bugs unrelated to theming — broken layout, a button that does nothing, a modal that doesn't close, text that's cut off, a state that never updates — note and fix anything you notice, not just color bugs.

WORKFLOW: for each page, log in via a Playwright script (must live under /opt/nxeon-v2/scripts/ per CLAUDE.md, e.g. scripts/_audit_a2.mjs — delete it when you're done, this repo's convention is not to leave one-off scripts lying around), screenshot in BOTH dark (default) and light mode (`localStorage.setItem('nx-theme','light'); document.documentElement.setAttribute('data-theme','light')` before navigating, same trick used everywhere else this session), actually LOOK at the screenshots (read them back as images), diagnose anything that looks wrong using the taxonomy above, fix it in the source, rebuild, re-screenshot to confirm the fix, then move to the next page. Run `cd /opt/nxeon-v2 && npx tsc --noEmit` after every batch of edits.

Don't invent problems that aren't there — several pages may already be fine (if a page already uses `.card`/`.card-glass`/tokens throughout, it likely needs nothing). Only fix what's actually visibly or functionally broken. Write a final report listing every bug found (with a short description and the file it was in) and every fix made, plus any page you found to already be correct.

#!/bin/bash
# Rebuild and restart the v2 sandbox.
#
# The tree runs a PRODUCTION build (`npm start`), not the dev server: ~0.8 GB
# instead of ~4.5 GB, on a box whose spare memory is measured against fifteen
# customer VMs. The cost is that nothing hot-reloads — every change needs this.
#
# WHY IT STOPS THE SERVER FIRST. `next build` writes into `.next`, which the
# running server is reading from. Building underneath a live server replaces the
# manifests it has open and every route starts returning 500 — this has already
# happened once in this tree. Stop, build, start. Never build in place.
set -euo pipefail

cd /opt/nxeon-v2
LOG=/tmp/nxeon-v2-build.log

# ── one build at a time ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Two concurrent runs write the same `.next` and corrupt it — the exact failure
# this script exists to prevent, arrived at from a different direction. It was
# survivable only by accident: the build runs inside a transient scope, and
# systemd refuses a second scope of the same name, so run two and the LOSER
# fails loudly. Relying on that is relying on a side effect of a name. This
# takes a real lock and says plainly what happened.
exec 9>/tmp/nxeon-v2-rebuild.lock
if ! flock -n 9; then
  echo "==> another rebuild is already running (holding /tmp/nxeon-v2-rebuild.lock)."
  echo "    Wait for it to finish — starting a second one would corrupt .next."
  exit 1
fi

# ── skip the marketing site ────────────────────────────────────────────────
# The redesign does not touch marketing, but it is ~137 of the ~195 route files
# and most of the 254 static pages, so it dominates a build we now run by hand
# after every change.
#
# Next excludes any folder whose name starts with `_` from routing, so renaming
# the route group is all it takes. This is a SANDBOX-ONLY, TEMPORARY rename: the
# trap puts it back whatever happens — including a failed build or a Ctrl-C — so
# git never sees it and nothing different is ever merged to prod.
#
# Set NX_FULL=1 to build the whole site (do this before any staging/prod pass,
# where marketing MUST be built and exercised).
MK="app/(marketing)"
MK_OFF="app/_marketing_skipped"
restore() { [ -d "$MK_OFF" ] && mv "$MK_OFF" "$MK"; }
trap restore EXIT INT TERM

if [ "${NX_FULL:-0}" != "1" ] && [ -d "$MK" ]; then
  echo "==> skipping the marketing site (NX_FULL=1 to include it)"
  mv "$MK" "$MK_OFF"
fi

echo "==> stopping the server (it reads .next; building under it breaks it)"
systemctl stop nxeon-v2-web

echo "==> building"
start=$(date +%s)
# Capped so a runaway build is killed rather than squeezing the customer VMs,
# and niced so it always yields to them.
if systemd-run --scope --quiet --unit=v2-rebuild \
     -p MemoryMax=6G -p MemorySwapMax=2G -p CPUWeight=30 \
     bash -c 'cd /opt/nxeon-v2 && export NEXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1 && set -a && . ./.env && set +a && npm run build' \
     > "$LOG" 2>&1; then
  echo "==> built in $(( $(date +%s) - start ))s"
else
  echo "!!! BUILD FAILED — the server is NOT being restarted on a broken build."
  echo "    Last 20 lines of $LOG:"
  tail -20 "$LOG"
  exit 1
fi

echo "==> starting"
systemctl start nxeon-v2-web
for _ in $(seq 1 60); do
  code=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' --max-time 20 http://127.0.0.1:3021/login || true)
  [ "$code" = "200" ] && { echo "==> up: /login $code"; exit 0; }
  sleep 2
done
echo "!!! server did not come up — check: journalctl -u nxeon-v2-web -n 40"
exit 1
